name: calculator
instructions:
Use calc_eval instead of working arithmetic out yourself — it is exact where you approximate, and a long calculation done in your head goes wrong in the middle without showing it.

Compose the WHOLE calculation into one expression: `(1847 * 0.0325) / 12`, not three calls with reasoning between them. That is what makes it worth calling at all.

`^` is exponentiation and binds right, so 2^3^2 is 512, not 64.

There is no `log` — use log10, loge, or logn(value, base). Reaching for `log` is a refusal, not a guess at which base you meant.

A refusal means there is no number, not that the call broke: division by zero and overflow come back as failures rather than as ∞, because ∞ carried into your next step becomes a wrong answer with no sign that it went wrong.

Results are double-precision. For money, do not use this.

tools.name: calc_eval
tools.description: Evaluates a mathematical expression exactly and returns the result. Takes one expression, however long — compose the whole calculation rather than calling repeatedly.
